findings.claim: T34 defines IsTaskNotification as 'starts with <task-notification> or contains [SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT]' anywhere in the prompt. A real user prompt that quotes or pastes that marker would silently skip codegraph. L88 rejects a shell match because it cannot tell the marker inside the prompt from elsewhere, yet the specified Go predicate also accepts the marker anywhere in the prompt text. The marker position is listed as unverified, so the over-match risk is not bounded.

A second '## Log' heading is added as a parser workaround. Nothing in the diff shows that tooling other than oddtask.ParseDocument (for example one that takes the first Log heading, or a duplicate-heading check) accepts two Log sections. Whether the L88 entry is read as the shaper's depends on unverified parser behavior.

evidence: Docs-only change to one feature document; the only checks possible were internal consistency (forecast sums, Risk lists and the wrapper shell precedence are consistent) and the parser claims the diff makes.
